summary: H.R. 10194, titled the Preventing Revenue Opportunities for Workplace Lockouts and Retaliation Act (or PRO–WORK Act), proposes changes to the National Labor Relations Act and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The bill stops employers engaged in employee lock-outs from receiving federal funds or tax credits for specific periods, and requires employers to reimburse the government for federal funds used during certain lock-out periods starting from January 1, 2026.

affected_groups.effect: Employers engaged in locking out employees are barred from accessing federal funds during and after the lock-out, must reimburse the government for past violations starting from January 1, 2026, and lose eligibility for certain corporate tax credits.

key_provisions: Prohibits making available, obligating, or expending any federal funds to an employer during a lock-out period and an additional matching period (or a 1-year period if there was a prior lock-out).

Requires employers to reimburse the Federal Government for any funds obligated or expended in violation of the funding ban during any lock-out period occurring between January 1, 2026, and the date of enactment.

Denies tax credits under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to corporations engaged in a lock-out of employees for the taxable year, to the extent allocable to the lock-out period or entirely for the taxable year in repeat cases.
Applies aggregation rules treating entities under common employer definitions as a single corporation for the tax credit denial.
Directs the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of Labor, to issue necessary regulations or guidance to carry out the tax credit provisions.

summary_detail.significance: The bill changes federal financial interactions with businesses by establishing financial penalties through the restriction of federal funds and tax credits for corporations involved in employee lock-outs.
